etymologies.etymologyHTML: From opportune +‎ -ity, from Middle French opportunité, from Latin opportunitas.

definitions.definition: A chance for advancement, progress or profit.

quote.citation: 1935, “letter”, in Department of science, art and literature: Hearings before the Committee on Patents, page 112:
quote.text: The chairman of the committee will be very glad to give you the opportunity to express your views, whether of proponency or opponency.

quote.citation: 1968, Leonard E. Goodall, The American Metropolis, page 5:
quote.text: Unfortunately, the job opportunities they are seeking are often more hoped for than real,  […]

quote.citation: 2011 October 23, Becky Ashton, “QPR 1 - 0 Chelsea”, in BBC Sport‎[1]:
quote.text: Chelsea also struggled to keep possession as QPR harried and chased at every opportunity, giving their opponents no time on the ball.
